scope: Guarded browser diagnostics of GUI in-place reopening of an exported original PLY-3 Split/Extract project; failure, not acceptance

runs.name: r3-remote-playwright-file
runs.observation: The 475566423-byte artifact was streamed to disk and Playwright selected it. The decoder started; the page crashed before a decoder result or replacement confirmation was recorded. The guarded process exited with failure and cleaned up.

runs.name: r4-direct-local-cdp-file
runs.observation: The same workflow selected the locally written file directly in the local browser using CDP, avoiding the remote Playwright file-copy path. The decoder started, but the completion wait and page-state probe timed out without a decoder result or confirmation. No crash event was observed before cleanup. The guarded process exited with failure and cleaned up.

interpretation: The direct-file failure means the remote Playwright file-copy path alone does not explain this result. The GUI and public MCP both invoke the shared project decoder, but the separately passing MCP in-place import does not establish GUI file-open success. The precise allocation or scheduling cause remains unproven.
limitations: The harness runs an isolated browser and retains the current scene during decode. The recorded job peak exceeded the nominal job limit; the guard reports successful cleanup, not acceptance.
The decoder did not report its internal stage before failure, so the evidence does not isolate file reads, decompression, reconstruction, browser memory accounting, or other process allocations.
The earlier r1 and r2 failures are retained in the same work directory; r2's post-timeout page-state probe also timed out. No production or MCP change is claimed.
